text:
Matvei Michkov might want out, and Philadelphia is arguing about it everywhere. ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported that the 21-year-old may want to play elsewhere, unhappy with the organization, after a season of questions about his ice time under Rick Tocchet. Travis Konecny was caught calling him out on the bench, a fan's billboard calling for Tocchet's firing made the rounds, and the Inquirer reported that GM Danny Briere has put his coach on notice.

The hockey isn't helping. The Flyers are 6-10-6 with 18 points, and they've taken 43% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances). Our playoff odds are at 4%. Saturday's 4-3 win in Columbus, where they came back from two down, was the first time all season they'd won a game that was tied at any point in the third, per PHLY's Charlie O'Connor, who has also written about how cautious they get late.

The irony is that Michkov is driving play when he's out there. His line with Noah Cates and rookie Porter Martone has taken 62% of the expected goals, the best numbers of any regular trio. He scored a dazzling individual goal in Columbus. Denver Barkey scored twice in that game, including the winner, and keeps earning more ice.

What we'd watch: whether Michkov's minutes go up, and whether the front office decides the coach or the player is the problem first.
